outputs_written: docs/blog/2026-08-08-two-things-were-stopping-you-from-making-a-character.md — W1-26-r3: creation soft-locked at the desk (New never observes a race; the caught throw's engine-error string was rendered as the scribe's own line, door held shut); input/real.js checked movement/control keys before the text field, dropping 14 of 26 letters and committing the name on E ('Silt-Under-Salt' -> 'il-Un', predicted from the key bindings then confirmed live twice). Both fixed, checked with real keyboard input; play.sh + README.md now at repo root. Balanced explicitly: ungraded by a fresh critic since the fix (one started 05:08 this morning, still running); orchestrator itself reproduced 2 of 3 acceptance tools, the third (full played opening) died at 3.74 sim fps under loadavg 20.9 — contention, not the build.

docs/blog/2026-08-08-a-body-walked-the-whole-province.md — W1-CROSSING: Stormhold-Lilmoth, 6,646.7 m / 199,433 frames / 55.398 min, settlement collision ON, 0 frames off-road, 0 teleports, all four RI-WLD01 bars pass, hour came from distance. Told as the three wrong readings first: 'Met' on a walker with no body; a real body stopped 39 m in at a house (10/10 road legs run through a building, generators never compared); a '57.5 deg skirt' that isn't real — worst road gradient anywhere is 24.27 deg vs a 40 deg limit, the reading was field.slopeAt() beside a 471 m/50.6 m viaduct, body 15.3 m below deck, fell off. Fix was walker steering, proved by a 2x2 that reproduces the old 550.1 m stall at the exact published coordinate with pre-fix code restored. Also filed: path_m had been counting hazard-respawn teleports as walked distance uncapped per-frame — flagged as putting earlier published distances in doubt.

docs/blog/2026-08-08-the-facility-built-to-catch-a-fake-control-had-one-of-its-own.md — W1-25-r1/r2: the sabotage-control facility, pointed at a real shipped control (W1-14-r3 nocast) a human had already ruled inert, returns OK or VACUOUS depending entirely on one optional caller-supplied integer that defaults to skipping the check; its own first live run canonicalised two undefined arms to 'agreement' and returned the flagship verdict INERT from a typo (misread field path). Round 2 makes the integer mandatory and quotes its own argument for why: {33/55} and {0/55} are byte-identical in shape to a known-good control at 67->0/360 — no rule over the numbers separates them, only the caller's declared meaning. Ungraded since r1's FAIL 2/10; matrix-probe.mjs still not run, demonstrated_crossings still 0/floor 4.

docs/blog/2026-08-08-a-third-of-every-edge-in-the-interface.md — W1-21-r3: FD6 (red round 1 unnamed, named-but-unresolved round 2) converted to its item's own ΔE2000 unit: worst edge 58.291, 14/14 captures over the hard-fail bar of 8, 31,322 of 98,659 graded edge pixels over the pass bar of 3 (31.7%) — caps RI-UIX06 fidelity at 2. Sibling: round 2's 12 old grading expressions, transcribed back in over an emptied sample set, all still return PASS (round 3's rewritten 25 checks all correctly report EMPTY under the identical test) — one of the 12 is the check that published 66 false 'damage number' hits off a frame with no hit landed. Map's markers field (a hand-typed literal 0 for two rounds) now derived from what's drawn. Ungraded — no fresh critic on round 3 yet.
